item.title: Pilot, copilot killed in collision between jet and fire truck at New York's LaGuardia Airport
item.description: The impact severed the cockpit, and hurled a flight attendant — still secured to her seat — far from the site of the crash, her daughter told a Canadian TV station. The flight attendant survived.

item.title: Multi-platinum artist Cole Swindell coming to The Mill
item.description: Cole Swindell is coming to Terre Haute for a show at The Mill on July 9, with tickets going on sale March 27.

item.title: Pocket Parks will soon be coming to Terre Haute
item.description: The City of Terre Haute is adding four pocket parks to the Terre Haute Green Pockets initiative, funded by federal money from the Inflation Reduction Act, to improve property appeal, stormwater management, walkability, public health, and provide outdoor green spaces for the community.

item.title: City of Terre Haute to hold city wide cleanup on April 11th
item.description: The City of Terre Haute is holding a city-wide cleanup event on April 11th, where people can bring in items to be disposed of and help out local non-profits, with Burkhart Insurance donating $10 for every bag of trash collected.

item.title: Indy 500 program visits local elementary school
item.description: Rio Grande Elementary in Terre Haute received a special visit from the 500 Festival and Indianapolis 500 Education Program, which provided students with an interactive experience to learn about the Indy 500 and its history.

item.title: ISU students bring home a national title
item.description: Indiana State University's Bailey College of Engineering and Technology's Construction Management Program won the national title at the Mechanical Contractors Association of America Student Chapter Competition, with Braidyn Hudson being named MVP presenter.

item.title: Senate passes new fentanyl bill
item.description: The Senate passed Tyler's Law unanimously, which will direct the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to provide hospitals with guidance on implementing fentanyl testing into routine ER drug screens, in an effort to prevent fentanyl poisoning tragedies.

item.title: New study shows Terre Haute housing stock is aging
item.description: According to a new study from Construction Coverage, the median age of homes in Terre Haute is 53 years old, which is 10 years older than the nation's median, and 61.6% of homes were built before 1980.
